name: error first callback
desc: The older async style: the last argument is a function, called once with an error or a result. Only one of the two is non null.
body: The `return` in the error branch is load bearing. Without it the success branch runs with a null result. Nesting several of these calls is what promises were invented to flatten.

name: new Promise()
desc: Creates a promise. The executor runs immediately and synchronously. A throw inside it rejects the promise.
body: A promise settles once. Calling `resolve` after `reject` or the reverse does nothing. Do not wrap a function that already returns a promise; return it unchanged.

name: Promise.resolve()
desc: Returns an already fulfilled promise. Useful as a default value or to start a chain with a known value.
example:
const start = Promise.resolve({ hotel_id: 1 });

start
  .then((hotel) => hotel.hotel_id)
  .then((id) => console.log(id)); // 1

name: .then()
desc: Registers handlers for success and failure and returns a new promise. The handler's return value becomes the next promise's value.
body: Returning a promise from `then` makes the chain wait for it. Forgetting the `return` in a handler written with braces passes `undefined` down the chain.

name: .catch()
desc: Handles a rejection from this promise or from any earlier link in the chain. It returns a new promise, so a handler that does not rethrow turns the chain back to fulfilled.

name: .finally()
desc: Runs on both outcomes and receives no argument. Use it for cleanup such as hiding a spinner. A value returned from it is ignored.

name: chaining
desc: Runs steps in order without nesting. An error skips every then until the next catch.
example:
loadHotel(7)
  .then((hotel) => loadOwner(hotel.owner_email))
  .then((owner) => console.log(owner.first_name))
  .catch((error) => console.error(error.message));

name: Promise.all()
desc: Waits for all promises and returns their values in input order. Rejects on the first rejection, and the other promises keep running.
body: Order comes from the input array, not from completion. `all` is the right tool when every result is required and one failure should stop the page.

name: Promise.allSettled()
desc: Waits for all promises and never rejects. Each result is { status: "fulfilled", value } or { status: "rejected", reason }.

name: Promise.race()
desc: Settles with the first promise that settles, success or failure. The slower promises keep running and their results are ignored.

name: async function
desc: Marks a function that always returns a promise and may use await inside. A returned value fulfils the promise, a thrown error rejects it.

name: await with try/catch
syntax: try { const value = await p; } catch (error) { ... }
desc: Turns a rejected promise into a caught exception. finally runs on both paths and is the place to reset loading state.

name: parallel await
desc: Two independent awaits in a row cost the sum of both waits. Start them together and await once to pay only the slower one.

name: fetch GET
desc: Sends a GET request and resolves with a Response. GET is the default method, and the body arrives in a second await.

name: fetch POST JSON
desc: Creates a resource. Needs the method, a JSON content type, and a string body. The server parses the body only when the type is correct.

name: fetch PUT and DELETE
desc: PUT replaces the whole resource. DELETE removes it and often answers 204 with no body, so do not parse it.

name: headers
desc: Sets request metadata. JSON bodies need Content-Type. Do not set it for FormData, because the browser adds the multipart boundary.

name: response.ok
desc: True for status 200 to 299. fetch does not reject on 404 or 500, so this check is the only thing between an error page and your render.

name: response.json()
desc: Reads and parses the body. The body can be read once, and a malformed body rejects with a SyntaxError.

name: AbortController
desc: Cancels an in flight request. The promise rejects with an error whose name is AbortError, which is not a failure to show the user.
body: Abort is also the cure for a stale search response. Keep one controller per view, call `abort()` when a new request starts, and compare a request token before rendering.

name: fetch error handling
desc: Separates three failures: a network rejection, an HTTP status with ok false, and a body parse error. Only the first reaches catch on its own.

name: loading and error state
desc: One object drives the screen: idle, loading, success, or error. Two booleans allow loading and error at the same time.
